lines.text: First-pass plan review for city building departments.
It reads a permit drawing set, follows every stair floor to floor, and drafts the correction letter. It never approves a plan.
Built on Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 and SAM 3.1
More than 80% of standard permit plans in Portland needed corrections.
Seattle's AI plan-check pilot passed 6.4% of the checks a human examiner sent back.
Nobody looks again at what was passed. Storey has no pass state at all.

cards.title: Measured on 33 sets, two held out until the code was frozen

lines.text: Generated sets: 184 of 184 planted and rule items raised. Spark asked directly: 81 of 177.
Findings with no cause: 15, against 161 for Spark asked directly.
Wrong passes on held-out stair cells: 1 of 16.
Real sets audited by hand: 6 of 121 items. Most are kinds no Storey check covers yet.
Draft for examiner. Not an approval.

captions.up1: Upload a permit set. This is The Capitol, a 22-sheet duplex from a public pattern book.
captions.up2: Muse Spark reads every sheet, orders the floors and follows each stair. This real run, sped up 16 times, took 3.3 minutes and cost 0.39 USD.
captions.up3: The result: a draft correction list, with the evidence for every item.
captions.st1: Every stair followed floor to floor. SAM 3.1 tracks each one through the stack and draws it.
captions.st2: No model decides alone. Spark is asked three times, then ink at the place and a blind crop question must agree.
captions.st3: Found means: 3 of 3 runs, ink at the place, and the crop said yes.
captions.te1: Test it live: remove the central stair from the second floor of a copy.
captions.te2: Storey runs the stair stage again on the copy. Sped up 20 times.
captions.te3: Must fix: Stair C is missing on the second floor. 0 of 3 runs, the crop said no, no ink at the place.
captions.fi1: Each item names the sheet, the place, what was read, what is needed, and why.
captions.fi2: Real drafting errors in a published set: this title block names the wrong floor.
captions.fi3: What Storey could not check is listed too. An unread item never becomes a pass.
captions.ci1: Houston: one stair cannot serve the fourth and fifth floors of this block.
captions.ci2: Switch to Seattle. The rules run again in a moment, with no model call, and its single-exit rule removes both items.
captions.se1: The resubmittal: each earlier comment is checked again at its place on the new set.
captions.se2: Looks resolved, Still open or Cannot tell, with the earlier and new drawing side by side.
captions.le1: The comment letter, drafted in the format cities already send. The examiner edits it and decides.
captions.ev1: The evaluation is published with its misses, both wrong passes included.

voice.card_title: Storey. First-pass plan review for city building departments, built on Meta's Muse Spark and SAM 3.1.
voice.card_problem: In Portland, eight in ten permit plans needed corrections. Seattle's own AI pilot passed six point four percent of the checks a human examiner sent back. Storey has no pass state at all.
voice.card_numbers: Measured on thirty-three sets, two held out until the code was frozen. Storey raised all one hundred and eighty-four generated items, Spark asked directly eighty-one, with ten times the false findings. One wrong pass in sixteen held-out stair cells. And real audits show the next step: more checks.
